hypothesis: The market impact should depend less on the headline $200bn/$54bn figures than on binding project approvals, annual cash-remittance timing, funding source, ownership/return structure and FX hedging. A staged, commercially conditional program can have materially smaller near-term USD/KRW and Korean-liquidity pressure than headline notional amounts imply, while still creating medium-term order opportunities for Korean power/nuclear/engineering supply chains.

If commercial returns and Korean equipment content are high, beneficiary order momentum could dominate macro leakage.
